one_liner: ByteDance's Go RPC framework whose gRPC-compatible transport, built on the Netpoll event loop, out-serves grpc-go on small unary RPCs.
what_it_does: Kitex is a full Go microservice RPC framework: a code generator for Thrift and Protobuf IDL (the kitex CLI), a client/server runtime, and pluggable governance such as discovery, load balancing, retry, circuit breaking, rate limiting and tracing. For gRPC it speaks standard gRPC over HTTP/2, so it can talk to grpc-go or Java gRPC peers. One server port auto-detects Thrift/TTHeader, gRPC and TTHeader streaming. The API is Kitex's own: generated xxx.NewClient/NewServer plus options such as client.WithTransportProtocol(transport.GRPC). It does not replace grpc.Dial or grpc.NewServer.
how_it_is_fast: The gRPC transport (pkg/remote/trans/nphttp2) is grpc-go v1.26.0's HTTP/2 transport, forked onto Netpoll. Netpoll is ByteDance's epoll/kqueue event-loop network library, and it replaces Go's net package, which blocks one goroutine per connection. Netpoll reads into LinkBuffer, a linked buffer built from pooled blocks. A fork of golang.org/x/net/http2's framer parses frames straight out of that buffer, reuses frame objects, and batches writes into a per-connection buffer (32KB by default, allocated at twice that size). The poller calls epoll_wait with timeout 0 while events keep arriving and -1 when idle; ByteDance measured this as about 18% cheaper per call. In the benchmark, the Kitex stubs also used fastpb-generated FastRead/FastWrite codecs, which compute the size first and then write, rather than the standard protoc-gen-go code.
when_to_use: Go services on Linux handling many small unary protobuf RPCs (around 1KB) where server CPU is the limit. With 4 server cores the benchmark showed 1.5-1.7x the QPS of grpc-go, and p99 fell from 3.15 to 1.73 ms at 100 concurrent callers.
You must stay on the gRPC wire protocol to interoperate with existing grpc-go or other-language clients, and you want governance (discovery, LB, retry, circuit breaking) built into the framework.

Streaming-heavy services: a December 2024 rerun against grpc-go v1.66.2 measured 1.33x the QPS of grpc-go streaming at 100 streams (377k vs 283k) while using less server CPU (296% vs 335%), and 1.42x at 1000 streams.
Organisations running Thrift and gRPC side by side that want one Go RPC stack and one server port for both.
when_not_to_use: Windows: Kitex falls back to Go's net package there because Netpoll does not support Windows. Maintainers say gRPC on Windows is unsupported, and an open issue (#1154) reports a server panic ('close of closed channel').

You need TLS or mTLS terminated in-process on the server. Netpoll has no TLS, the FAQ says Kitex does not natively support TLS, and there is no server gRPC TLS option. Maintainers point to an Envoy sidecar or to switching the server to the gonet transport, which gives up Netpoll. Clients get TLS only through WithGRPCTLSConfig.
Tail-latency-sensitive streaming at high fan-in: in the 2024 streaming CSV, Kitex's p99 is higher than grpc-go's from 400 concurrent streams up (8.12 vs 6.16 ms at 1000).
proto2 schemas: Kitex's Protobuf support is proto3-only.
Code built around grpc-go's API (grpc.Dial, grpc.NewServer, its ServerOptions and interceptors). Stubs must be regenerated with the kitex tool, and middleware must be ported to Kitex's model.

integration.dependencies: cloudwego/netpoll, bytedance/gopkg, bytedance/sonic, cloudwego/frugal, fastpb, prutal, dynamicgo, thriftgo, golang.org/x/net, google.golang.org/protobuf and more (see go.mod). Code generation needs the kitex CLI plus protoc (Protobuf) or thriftgo (Thrift).
integration.min_toolchain: Go 1.20 (go.mod directive); the docs promise support for the latest three Go releases
integration.platforms: Linux and macOS use Netpoll (epoll/kqueue). Windows compiles and runs since v0.4.0 but uses Go net, and gRPC there is unsupported per maintainers (issue #1154). CPU architecture limits are not documented.
integration.thread_safety: A client object is safe for concurrent use and should be created once per downstream service and cached (docs warn against a client per request). RPCInfo is pooled via sync.Pool and must not be used after the handler returns; use rpcinfo.FreezeRPCInfo or KITEX_DISABLE_RPCINFO_POOL=true.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it is wire-compatible with gRPC over HTTP/2, but you regenerate stubs with the kitex tool and program against Kitex's client/server API and middleware instead of grpc-go's

gotchas: A Kitex Protobuf client sends Kitex Protobuf, not gRPC, unless the IDL has streaming methods or you set client.WithTransportProtocol(transport.GRPC). Pointing a default Kitex client at a grpc-go server therefore fails.

The HTTP/2 transport is a 2019-era fork (grpc-go v1.26.0 transport; x/net/http2 framer from Go 1.17.4), so upstream fixes do not arrive automatically. Open reports include streams stuck in flow control (writeQuota.get) and Send returning nil on a dead peer (#1865, v0.14.1). Server panics on client disconnect were reported through v0.11.3 (#974).

FastWrite computes the message size first and then serialises into a buffer of that size. If another goroutine mutates a request or response object in between, you get index-out-of-range or nil-pointer panics inside generated fastWriteField code; the docs classify this as a data race in user code that FastWrite exposes.
The client keeps GOMAXPROCS*3/2 HTTP/2 connections per target by default (grpc-go uses one ClientConn). The docs warn that resizing it with WithGRPCConnPoolSize can hurt performance.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among Go options, pick Kitex over rpcx (its own binary protocol) or cmd-stream (MUS codec) when callers must keep speaking standard gRPC. Those siblings post bigger margins over grpc-go but abandon the gRPC wire format. wtx reports larger gains as a gRPC server but is Rust, and brpc and grpcxx are C++, so Kitex is the pick for a gRPC-compatible Go stack with governance included.
verified_claims_summary: In ByteDance's own kitex-benchmark (data from August 2022), a Kitex server on its gRPC transport was compared with a default grpc.NewServer() from grpc-go v1.42.0 on a 1KB protobuf echo. Both were built with Go 1.17.2 and default flags, on a Xeon Gold 5118 with the server pinned to 4 CPUs and the client to 16 on the same host over loopback. Kitex served 156,167 vs 103,178 QPS at 100 concurrent callers (1.51x) and 193,971 vs 114,054 at 1000 (1.70x). The Kitex side also used fastpb-generated codecs against standard protoc-gen-go code, so the measured gain is transport plus codec, not transport alone.
status_note: Actively developed (v0.16.2 in May 2026, commits through 2026-09-22), Apache-2.0 and consumed as a normal Go module. However, the published unary gRPC numbers were last regenerated in August 2022; only the streaming comparison was rerun, in December 2024.
